title: Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, Archangels
short_summary: The feast of Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael honors the three angels named in Scripture. Michael appears as a defender of God's people, Gabriel announces God's saving purposes, and Raphael accompanies and heals in the Book of Tobit.
key_facts: The Roman calendar celebrates the three archangels together as a feast on September 29.
Michael is named in Daniel, Jude, and Revelation.
Gabriel appears in Daniel and announces the births of John the Baptist and Jesus in Luke.
Raphael identifies himself in Tobit as one of the seven angels who stand before God.

sections.heading: Angels in Catholic teaching
sections.body: The Church teaches that angels are spiritual creatures created by God. They possess intelligence and will, serve the divine plan, and direct their ministry toward Christ. The word angel describes their office as messengers rather than their nature. Scripture depicts them worshiping God, announcing his acts, protecting his people, and assisting the mission of salvation.

sections.heading: Michael
sections.body: Michael's name asks, 'Who is like God?' In Daniel he is the great prince associated with the defense of Israel. The Letter of Jude calls him an archangel, and Revelation portrays Michael and his angels fighting the dragon. Christian tradition therefore invokes him especially in relation to spiritual conflict and the protection of the Church.

sections.heading: Gabriel
sections.body: Gabriel interprets visions for Daniel and stands at the beginning of Luke's Gospel. He announces the birth of John the Baptist to Zechariah and the conception of Jesus to Mary. His greeting at the Annunciation became part of the Hail Mary, making his words among the most frequently repeated angelic speech in Christian prayer.

sections.heading: Raphael
sections.body: Raphael accompanies Tobias in the Book of Tobit under the appearance of a human traveler. He guides the journey, helps bring about the marriage of Tobias and Sarah, binds the demon Asmodeus, and directs the healing of Tobit's blindness. His name means 'God heals,' and he became associated with travelers, healing, and marriage.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Servants of Christ
catholic_connection_sections.body: Catholic devotion to angels is ordered to God. The angels have no independent divine power; their dignity and activity come from the Creator, and their work serves the kingdom of Christ.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Named by Scripture
catholic_connection_sections.body: The Latin Church ordinarily uses the names Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael because these are the angelic names given in canonical Scripture. Their distinct biblical missions provide the substance of the feast.

historical_cautions: Avoid assigning names to other angels from apocryphal or esoteric traditions as though they held the same scriptural and liturgical standing.
Artistic depictions give angels human bodies and wings as symbols; Catholic teaching describes them as spiritual, non-corporeal creatures.
